# Checklists {#sec-listas}

Short lists to keep at hand. You can print them or copy them into your notes.

## Before believing or sharing something

- [ ] Do I know who is behind the source? (If not, find out away from the page: lateral reading.)
- [ ] What are their interests: to inform, sell, persuade?
- [ ] Do other reliable, independent sources report it, or do they all copy the same thing?
- [ ] Have I got to the original source (the study, the data, the law)?
- [ ] Does the headline say the same as the original, or does it exaggerate?
- [ ] Does the date matter? Is it still valid?

## Before you start searching

- [ ] I have written my question in one sentence.
- [ ] I have separated the concepts and have synonyms and variants for each.
- [ ] I have decided the limits: dates, languages, document types.
- [ ] I know which platforms I will use and why.
- [ ] I have somewhere to note the strategy and the results.

## Before submitting an assignment

- [ ] Every idea, figure or piece of data from others has its in-text citation.
- [ ] Every citation in the text has its reference, and vice versa.
- [ ] Quotations are in quotation marks and have a page number.
- [ ] I have used a single citation style, consistently.
- [ ] I have checked the references generated by the reference manager.
- [ ] Images that are not mine have an author and a licence.
- [ ] I have declared the use of AI, if there was any and the course requires it.

## Before using generative AI

- [ ] I know what the teaching staff allow in this activity.
- [ ] I will not enter personal data or confidential documents.
- [ ] I will verify every fact and every reference it gives me.
- [ ] I review, understand and take responsibility for the final result.
- [ ] I note the tool, the version and what I use it for, in case I need to declare it.
